correctness.rationale: Every leading Schur complement \(S\) of an SPD matrix satisfying \(\mu I\preceq A\preceq LI\) obeys the same enclosure \(\mu I\preceq S\preceq LI\), by the variational characterization of the Schur complement. Any current multiplier is an off-diagonal-to-diagonal ratio in a \(2\times2\) SPD principal block of \(S\). If that block has eigenvalue ratio \(q\), direct rotation of its eigenbasis gives the exact maximum \((q-1)/(2\sqrt q)\), attained at \(	an\theta=1/\sqrt q\). Since \(q\le\kappa\) and the maximum increases with \(q\), the claimed bound follows at every stage. The explicit family \(A_\kappa\) attains equality and yields a tie at \(\kappa=3+2\sqrt2\) and a forced swap above it.

originality.rationale: The classical facts that SPD Gaussian elimination needs no pivoting, that partial pivoting chooses a maximal column entry, and that partial pivoting bounds multipliers by one are treated as prior work. Broyden's full paper explicitly defines 'partially pivoted' matrices as those needing no row interchanges and studies condition numbers of the factors, but no SPD spectral-condition-number threshold or sharp multiplier formula was located. Higham's full overview states that SPD matrices need no pivoting but does not classify when a generic GEPP implementation actually leaves the permutation equal to the identity. Higham and Higham's full pivot-growth paper likewise does not contain this SPD frontier. Targeted database and exact-constant searches found no implication-equivalent statement.
residual_risks: The sharp multiplier inequality may have appeared in older LU/Cholesky literature as a specialized consequence of Kantorovich-type inequalities under terminology not captured by the searches.
A source may state the same threshold as a criterion for identity permutation under partial pivoting without using the phrase 'row-swap frontier'.
The equality case depends on tie policy; the tie-independent universal guarantee is strict below the frontier.

value.rationale: For SPD matrices it is classical that pivoting is unnecessary, but general-purpose LU codes may still execute the partial-pivot search and can in fact swap rows, thereby discarding symmetry and changing storage or sparsity patterns. The theorem gives the exact condition-number regime in which this cannot happen, together with a sharp dimension-free bound on every elimination multiplier and a minimal \(2\times2\) obstruction above the boundary. This cleanly separates stability of unpivoted SPD elimination from the actual permutation decisions made by GEPP.
